title: bug: the image is built from the approved SHA but migrations run from the working tree, so a deploy can apply migration files the image does not carry
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a from an external review (finding 5), VERIFIED at HEAD fee4e168 and reproduced through the REAL chain (real image builder + real migrateWithBackup + real nodeMigrationPorts().apply through the verifier-process-runner + real SqliteEventStore receipt) — not a hand-built port. Correctness refuter failed to refute. Severity refuter lowered it to MEDIUM: the migration workspace is MOE_DEPLOY_BUILD_CONTEXT (daemon-command-async-entries.ts:251) and NOTHING shipped sets it (scripts/up.ps1 does not), so the path is default-unreachable today, human-only, and recoverable via the pre-migration dump. Latent, but it must be closed before real deploys are trusted, and the migration RECEIPT lies about provenance when it fires.

MECHANISM (six files byte-identical between 51c4a004 and HEAD):
- IMAGE SIDE, immutable: deploy-image-build.ts:29-30 `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` must equal request.sha; :34-38 bare temp repo with objects/info/alternates; :62 `git archive --format=tar <sha>` piped into `docker build -` (:68-77). deploy-service.ts:279 `ports.build({ context, sha, tag })`.
- MIGRATION SIDE, working tree: deploy-command.ts:276-280 resolveDeployMigrationContext({ projectRoot: options.buildContext, workspace: options.buildContext }, { environment, requestId, sha }) — `sha` is passed but only lands in the receipt. deploy-migration-context.ts:127-136 the only workspace guard is `named !== workspace`, a PATH string compare, and `request.workspace` is passed by NEITHER production caller (deploy-command.ts:280, rollback-restore.ts:130-133) — so the DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH guard whose comment (:129-131) claims to prevent "migrating a different tree than the one the deploy archived" is DEAD. migration-service.ts:66 `ports.apply(input.workspace, input.databaseUrl)`; the sha is regex-validated (:41-42) and used only for replay conflict (:90-92); :46 the receipt durably records `sha: input.sha` even when the files came from HEAD or dirt. migration-ports.ts:40/:53 discover migrations/ from process.cwd(); :70-76 runs the child with cwd = the raw build-context tree.
- Partial mitigations that exist: the sha must be a commit OF the build-context repo (DEPLOY_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE), so skew is bounded to same-repo different-revision-or-dirty; migrateWithBackup dumps first (:64-65) and migrate_down exists; node-pg-migrate checkOrder:true catches out-of-order files but not newer-than-image files. The mis-recorded receipt sha misleads the down leg's `source.sha !== receipt.sha` checks (migrate-down-command.ts:61,65).

FIX SHAPE: pin the migration SOURCE to the built sha at the seam that already owns "which tree" — MigrationPorts.apply in migration-ports.ts — not at the deploy edge. Keep cwd = workspace so `import.meta.resolve('node-pg-migrate')` still finds the installed tool, but extract migrations/ for input.sha into a temp dir via the same isolated-object-store recipe deploy-image-build.ts:29-38 uses (`git archive <sha> migrations/` from a bare temp repo with alternates), hand that path to the child as an env variable, and change migration-ports.ts:40/:53 (and migration-down-ports.ts:79) to read from it instead of process.cwd(). MigrationInput.sha (migration-service.ts:17) already carries the value; execute() at :66 passes it through. The temp extract is torn down on every exit path (epic rail 4). Cheaper interim guard if the extract is out of scope: in resolveDeployMigrationContext, before the delivery read, `git -C <workspace> diff --quiet <sha> -- migrations` plus an untracked check under migrations/, refusing with the existing-but-dead DEPLOY_MIGRATION_WORKSPACE_MISMATCH (reword its :47-48 detail) — this makes the :129-131 comment true and keeps the refuse-before-any-effect ordering deploy-service.ts:305-309 relies on.

| input | answer |
| real repo, real sha, `migrations` | `OK`, files `['1700000000000-initial.js']`, bytes `"committed\n"` (tree held `"dirty\n"`) |

The `:61` stack-frame regex is UNCHANGED and still matches, because the extract's leaf directory is literally `migrations`.

Extraction runs in the PARENT before the runner is constructed: mkdir `<workspace>/.moe-next` recursive, `mkdtempSync` a `migration-source-` sibling, `extractCommittedPath(nodeGitRunner, {repository: workspace, sha, path: "migrations", destination})`. The mkdir/mkdtemp setup is wrapped in the same throw, so a workspace that cannot host the extract answers like any other failed apply rather than escaping as a raw fs error.

It is try/caught, so a teardown error can never replace the migration's answer. `sweepStaleSources` removes leftover `migration-source-*` siblings at the START of apply; it is best-effort in two layers (a missing metadata directory and an unremovable entry are both swallowed) because a stale extract is litter, not a failure, and both callers hold the project-wide `.migration.lock` so no live extract is ever a sibling.
